what: Replace the closing sentence 'Deleting one single item is NOT built yet — never promise it.' with a true one naming what CAN be erased singly: a fact, a saved note, a recorded relationship, a contact removed from the network, and the confirmation step before a permanent erase. 1,332 -> 1,532 characters. Nothing else in the text is touched, including the 'Data page in your profile' screen name, which is a separate open question waiting on Lika.
why: It is false, and it is false in the one answer people read before deciding whether to hand over their phonebook. The seat proved it on 20 September in four turns on one thread: at 04:15 the product said 'deleting a single item isn't supported yet, so if you want something gone it's whole-account deletion'; at 04:17, after saving a fact and asking for that one fact to be forgotten, it asked for confirmation ('this can't be undone') and then said 'Done, that note is permanently erased.' Two minutes, one thread, the same assistant. forget_contact_fact calls hardDeleteOwnFact behind an explicit confirmed=true gate; forget_user_note, forget_contact_relationship and remove_contact_from_network exist beside it. The capability is built, the product knows it is built, and this sentence tells somebody their only way out is to destroy the whole account. THE TEXT ALSO CONTRADICTS ITSELF: two sentences earlier it already says a fact can be retracted and stops being shown anywhere. APPLIED 20 September after Misho's delegation. Chosen first among everything he handed me because it is the only open item with a running cost: it is a false sentence on a live route, in the answer a person reads before deciding whether to hand over their phonebook, and every day it stands it tells somebody their only way out is to destroy the whole account.
